meta_description: Edens Edge Landscaping is a gardener in Romsey offering fixed prices with no hidden costs. Get your free quote today.
loc_hero_h1: Gardener Services in and around Romsey
loc_hero_intro: [CV: company_name] is a gardener in Romsey, taking on everything from a simple tidy up to a full makeover with groundwork, patios and decking. Every price we give is fixed, with no hidden costs.
loc_services_intro: Romsey gardens run from deep lawns by the river to small terrace yards. Homeowners here look for lawn care, groundwork, patios, decking and tree work, and the cards below show what each kind of work covers.

cards.card_text: Borders lost under weeds and grass that's got ahead of you make a garden feel neglected fast. Our [gardening](/locations/romsey/gardener) work is the upkeep that brings a garden back under control. It clears the beds and sharpens the edges, so the whole garden looks cared for again.

Is the garden awkward to use, with a slope that makes every trip down it a chore? The [landscape gardening](/locations/romsey/landscape-gardener) we do reshapes the ground itself, changing levels and surfaces so the garden is easy to move around and sit out in.

Garden design suits a garden that never quite worked, such as a back door opening onto nothing or a corner nobody uses. In a [garden design](/locations/romsey/landscape-designer) job, we start from how you'd like to use the space, then lay out the lawn, paths and seating around that.

People usually call about a tree after a winter gale drops a limb, or when branches start shading the house. Our [tree surgery](/locations/romsey/tree-service) jobs cover pruning, felling and stump removal, from trimming one heavy limb to taking down a whole tree.

Rushed paving leaves ragged cuts, uneven edges and a surface that never looks finished, however good the slabs were. When you're booking [paving](/locations/romsey/paving-contractor), the work covers the groundwork and the surface, whether it's for sitting out, parking or a route to the shed.

A deck you can step onto from the kitchen door and sit out on in the evenings is the result people are after. Our [decking](/locations/romsey/deck-builder) service covers new installation, repairs and restoration, so a tired deck can be rescued as well as a new one built.

loc_content_body:
Romsey sits low beside the River Test, and that shapes the work of any gardener in Romsey. Housing climbs to flatter ground to the east, away from the water. Gardens near the water come with old trees and changing levels to plan for. Up on the plateaux the ground is easier to lay out, and lawns, paths and boundaries take most of the attention.

In Whitenap, the older Botley Road houses keep deep gardens with mature oaks and hedgerows, which means a lot more lawn and boundary than the smaller estate fronts nearby. The late 1970s terraces at Five Elms have rear boundaries facing public areas, which makes a sound fence matter more. In the Old Town, the generous riverbank gardens at The Causeway sit right beside the water. Levels and established trees shape what can be built there.

Some gardens here are long and open, others tight and overlooked, and no two jobs look alike. We're family run and independent, with a team of [CV: team_size]. Where lawns and hedges need regular attention, our [gardening](/locations/romsey/gardener) covers it. Sloping ground, steps and retaining walls are a job for [landscape gardening](/locations/romsey/landscape-gardener), and heavy limbs over a roof or fence call for [tree surgery](/locations/romsey/tree-service).

If one of these sounds like your garden, ask for a quote and we'll go from there.

block4.card_body: A lawn beside a stream that stays soggy for days after rain is common here. Some gardens sit near the Test and others near the Tadburn. The fields to the west hold floodwater too, so how wet a garden gets depends on the street. Any job that goes into the ground has to be planned around that wetness.

block4.card_title: Boundaries as old as the houses
block4.card_body: Panels that lean, posts soft at the base and a garden wall with a bow in it usually belong to the original boundary. Romsey's post war estates and older streets were fenced when they were built, so those runs have had decades of weather. Replacing one means new posts and panels, or rebuilding the wall.

block4.card_title: Trees that have outgrown the garden
block4.card_body: Roots lifting a path and branches over the roof usually mean a tree planted for a bigger garden than this one. Mature trees in the older, larger gardens are the clearest example. Before a protected tree is touched, a few checks usually apply, so a tree surgeon should ask about them first.

block4.card_title: Front gardens turned over to parking
block4.card_body: Terraces with no drive are why so many front gardens get paved over for parking, and a paved front sends its rain straight to the road or next door. A new hard surface there usually needs to let rain soak through, or drain inside the garden rather than into the street.

loc_block5_h2: What Affects the Cost of Landscaping in Romsey
loc_cost_intro: What a landscaping job costs in Romsey comes down to the hours of work and what has to be carried or cleared. The four points below are the ones that usually add or save time here.

block5.card_title: Getting in on a terraced street
block5.card_body: On terraced streets such as those around Riverside Gardens and Rivermead Close, there's no vehicle access outside the front door. Materials are carried in by hand and any skip sits on the road, and all that carrying adds time to a job.

A garden that falls or rises from the house needs its levels taken, steps or a retaining edge, and more digging than a flat one. Streets east of the river rise up the valley sides, so sloping gardens are part of the picture here.

Where a conservation area applies, trees, front boundaries and ground surfaces usually get extra scrutiny. The checks and paperwork before work starts add time to a job, and some changes can't be made at all.

block5.card_title: What the last owner left behind
block5.card_body: Old concrete, a shed base, buried rubble or an overgrown hedge has to come out and go in a skip before anything new goes in. Older gardens carry more of it, simply because they've had more owners and more projects.

faq_items.faq_question: How much does landscaping cost in Romsey?
faq_items.faq_answer: Price follows the size of the job, the ground and the way in. A patio with steps and a retaining wall takes longer than a short path, and a garden reached only through the house takes longer again. Quotes are free. Groundwork on sloping or awkward gardens falls under [landscape gardening](/locations/romsey/landscape-gardener).

faq_items.faq_question: How soon can you get to Romsey?
faq_items.faq_answer: Our usual start is the [CV: start_time], and that holds across the whole town. A full garden makeover or a patio with steps needs more planning than a quick tidy. Frozen or waterlogged ground can also push groundwork back, so the sooner you ask, the sooner it's in the diary.

Yes, we're insured up to £[CV: insurance_cover]. The cover relates to the landscaping work we carry out, from groundwork and paving to fencing and tree work. Ask us about it whenever you like, before a job is agreed.

faq_items.faq_question: What happens when I ask for a quote in Romsey?
faq_items.faq_answer: You tell us about the garden, and we come back with a price. Where it is and what you'd like done are enough for us to begin. From there, we talk through the figure together and settle a date for the work to begin.

faq_items.faq_question: When is the best time of year for landscaping work?
faq_items.faq_answer: Hard landscaping runs most of the year, and planting and turf suit autumn and spring. Digging and building need ground that isn't frozen or sodden, so dry spells matter there. Seed, turf and new plants need mild, moist weather to root. If you want spring work, booking ahead helps.
